definition: Hybrid machine translation is a method of machine translation that is characterized by the use of multiple machine translation approaches within a single machine translation system.
details: The motivation for developing hybrid machine translation systems stems from the failure of any single technique to achieve a satisfactory level of accuracy. Many hybrid machine translation systems have been successful in improving the accuracy of the translations, and there are several popular machine translation systems which employ hybrid methods.

explainer.lead: Hybrid machine translation combines multiple translation approaches inside one system because no single technique reaches satisfactory accuracy alone. It matters as a practical way to patch the weaknesses of each method.

tiers.eli5: It is like translating with both a dictionary-lookup helper and a meaning-focused helper, then merging their work to get a better result.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers combine, for example, rule-based or statistical components with neural ones in a single pipeline; the pitfall is that the combination adds complexity and the gains depend on how well the components' outputs are merged.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as a machine translation method characterized by using multiple translation approaches within a single system. The motivation is the failure of any single technique to reach satisfactory accuracy; several popular systems use such hybrid methods, but no formal guarantee of improvement is given.

explainer.example: A system uses a rule-based component for terminology and a data-driven component for fluent phrasing, then selects among their outputs for the final translation.
